  1. Autoscaling

Autoscaling

Fixed replicas for LLM workloads

replicas sets a constant count. It is rendered only when scaling is absent.

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    replicas: 3
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"

Change the default for all entries:

llmDefaults:
  replicas: 2

Autoscaling LLM workloads

Setting scaling removes replicas from the rendered resource and hands control to the autoscaler.

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    scaling:
      minReplicas: 1
      maxReplicas: 8
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"

replicas and scaling are mutually exclusive in this chart. When scaling is present, any replicas value is ignored.

Scale to zero 

    scaling:
      minReplicas: 0
      maxReplicas: 4

Scaling to zero frees GPUs between requests, but the next request pays the full cold start: pod scheduling, image pull, model download, and engine warm-up. That is often minutes for a large model. Combine it with Local model cache to reduce the download portion.

Request-driven scaling

The LLM controller can scale on serving signals rather than CPU. The exact keys depend on the autoscaling stack installed in your cluster, so consult the CRD:

kubectl explain llminferenceservice.spec.scaling --recursive

An example using a workload autoscaler block:

    scaling:
      minReplicas: 1
      maxReplicas: 10
      wva:
        targetValue: "8"
        metric: waiting_requests

Install the KEDA and OpenTelemetry components that the metric source requires. Related upstream settings:

kserve-resources:
  kserve:
    opentelemetryCollector:
      scrapeInterval: 5s
      metricReceiverEndpoint: keda-otel-scaler.keda.svc:4317
      metricScalerEndpoint: keda-otel-scaler.keda.svc:4318

Autoscaling classic inference services

models entries render scaling fields directly.

models:
  - name: sentiment
    runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver
    modelFormat: huggingface
    storageUri: hf://distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english
    minReplicas: 2
    maxReplicas: 8
    scaleMetric: concurrency
    scaleTarget: 80
    containerConcurrency: 4
    timeout: 120
Field Purpose
minReplicas Lower bound; 0 enables scale to zero
maxReplicas Upper bound
scaleMetric concurrency, rps, cpu, or memory
scaleTarget Target value for the chosen metric
containerConcurrency Hard concurrent request limit per replica
timeout Request timeout in seconds
canaryTrafficPercent Traffic share for a new revision
deploymentStrategy Rollout strategy

scaleMetric accepts only the four values above; the schema rejects anything else.

Shared defaults 

modelDefaults:
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 4
  scaleMetric: concurrency
  scaleTarget: 100

A per-model value replaces the default:

models:
  - name: steady
    storageUri: s3://models/steady/v1

  - name: bursty
    storageUri: s3://models/bursty/v1
    minReplicas: 2
    maxReplicas: 20

Scale to zero 

models:
  - name: batch-scorer
    storageUri: s3://models/batch/v1
    minReplicas: 0
    maxReplicas: 4

minReplicas: 0 is rendered as 0 rather than being treated as unset, so scale to zero works as written.

Scale to zero requires a serverless-capable deployment mode. On the Standard deployment mode a Deployment cannot scale below one replica, so confirm the mode before relying on it:

kserve-resources:
  kserve:
    controller:
      deploymentMode: Standard

Controller-wide defaults

Stabilization windows are set once for the whole cluster:

kserve-resources:
  kserve:
    autoscaler:
      scaleUpStabilizationWindowSeconds: "0"
      scaleDownStabilizationWindowSeconds: "300"

Cluster autoscaling

Pod autoscaling only helps when nodes exist. For GPU workloads, pair it with a cluster autoscaler or Karpenter pool that can add GPU nodes, and confirm:

  • The node pool has a maximum size above your maxReplicas GPU demand.
  • Scale-down rules tolerate long model downloads.
  • The GPU device plugin runs on newly created nodes.

Choosing a strategy

Workload Recommendation
Interactive chat, steady traffic minReplicas: 2 to avoid cold starts
Interactive chat, spiky traffic scaling with request-based metric
Batch or offline scoring minReplicas: 0, high maxReplicas
Development and test replicas: 1
Strict latency targets Fixed replicas, no scale to zero

Verifying 

kubectl get llminferenceservice llama-8b -n models -o yaml | grep -A5 scaling
kubectl get hpa -n models
kubectl get pods -n models -w
kubectl top pods -n models
